3	/// The commit sheet's target, carried the way `PendingVCSAction` carries a confirmation's.
4	///
5	/// `.sheet(item:)` keys on `id`, so the sheet's `@State` — the draft and the selection — is rebuilt
6	/// per target and can never leak from one workroom into another.
7	struct PendingCommit: Identifiable, Equatable, Sendable {
8	  let sid: SidebarID
9	  /// `"git"` or `"jj"`. Decides whether per-file selection is offered at all and which second verb
10	  /// the menu carries.
11	  let vcs: String
12	  var id: String { "\(vcs)-\(sid.hashValue)" }
13	}
14	
15	/// The commit sheet's pure logic: what the message is, what is selected, and what the button says.
16	///
17	/// Separated from the view for the reason `ChangeBadge` and `VCSSyncPresenter` are: these are
18	/// many-case decisions that drift silently, and none of them is reachable from a test through
19	/// SwiftUI. The view holds state and renders; every rule below is decided here.
20	enum CommitDraft {
21	
22	  /// Compose the message git or jj will record.
23	  ///
24	  /// Summary and body are joined by a BLANK line, which is the convention every tool downstream
25	  /// relies on to split a subject from its body. Both halves are trimmed, and an empty body yields a
26	  /// subject-only message with no trailing newlines for `--cleanup` to strip.
27	  static func message(summary: String, body: String) -> String {
28	    let subject = summary.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
29	    let detail = body.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
30	    return detail.isEmpty ? subject : "\(subject)\n\n\(detail)"
31	  }
32	
33	  /// The message to record, preserving `original` byte for byte when neither field was edited.
34	  ///
35	  /// `split` and `message` are deliberately not inverses: `split` takes line 0 as the summary and the
36	  /// rest as the body, while `message` always rejoins them with a BLANK line. So a stored jj
37	  /// description of `"one\ntwo"` — no blank separator, which jj permits — came back as
38	  /// `"one\n\ntwo"`. The user pressed Describe without touching the text and their message changed
39	  /// underneath them.
40	  ///
41	  /// Normalising is right for a message the user actually wrote here (the blank line is what every
42	  /// tool downstream splits on). Rewriting one they didn't touch is not. This tells the two apart.
43	  static func message(summary: String, body: String, preserving original: String?) -> String {
44	    guard let original else { return message(summary: summary, body: body) }
45	    let stored = split(message: original)
46	    guard stored.summary == summary, stored.body == body else {
47	      return message(summary: summary, body: body)
48	    }
49	    return original
50	  }
51	
52	  /// Split a stored message back into the two fields, for prefilling from jj's `@` description.
53	  ///
54	  /// The first line is the summary and everything after the first blank line is the body. Used
55	  /// against the FULL description — `JJCommitChanges.description` carries only the first line, so
56	  /// prefilling from that and describing again would silently discard the body.
57	  static func split(message: String) -> (summary: String, body: String) {
58	    let normalized = message.replacingOccurrences(of: "\r\n", with: "\n")
59	    var lines = normalized.split(separator: "\n", omittingEmptySubsequences: false).map(String.init)
60	    guard !lines.isEmpty else { return ("", "") }
61	    let summary = lines.removeFirst().trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
62	    let body = lines.joined(separator: "\n").trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
63	    return (summary, body)
64	  }
65	
66	  /// The files a commit would record, given what the user has EXCLUDED.
67	  ///
68	  /// Deselections are stored, never selections, and this is the reason. Coding agents run in this
69	  /// app's own embedded terminals and write files continuously, so the change set moves underneath
70	  /// an open dialog. With a set of *selected* paths there are only two possible behaviours when a new
71	  /// path appears — include it silently (committing a file nobody reviewed, which is the exact defect
72	  /// per-file selection exists to prevent) or reset the selection (throwing away the user's
73	  /// deliberate exclusions). Storing exclusions makes a new file arrive checked, which is the honest
74	  /// default, and makes an exclusion survive every refresh.
75	  ///
76	  /// A path that vanishes from the change set drops out on its own, so the excluded set never needs
77	  /// pruning.
78	  static func selected(from files: [ChangedFile], excluding excluded: Set<String>) -> [ChangedFile]
79	  {
80	    files.filter { !excluded.contains($0.path) }
81	  }
82	
83	  /// The primary button's label. Names the count so what is about to be recorded is never implicit —
84	  /// once the list scrolls, "Commit" alone is an unverifiable claim.
85	  static func commitLabel(selectedCount: Int, vcs: String) -> String {
86	    // jj commits the whole change and offers no per-file selection, so a count would imply a choice
87	    // that isn't on offer.
88	    guard vcs != "jj" else { return "Commit" }
89	    switch selectedCount {
90	    case 1: return "Commit 1 file"
91	    default: return "Commit \(selectedCount) files"
92	    }
93	  }
94	
95	  /// Why Commit is unavailable, as a sentence, or nil when it is available.
96	  ///
97	  /// Returned as text rather than a Bool because these must render as a persistent inline line: four
98	  /// different blocked states explained only by a tooltip would be invisible to anyone who doesn't
99	  /// hover a control that already looks dead, and unavailable to VoiceOver entirely.
100	  static func blockedReason(
101	    vcs: String, summary: String, selectedCount: Int, totalCount: Int, conflicted: Bool,
102	    sequencer: String?
103	  ) -> String? {
104	    if let reason = repoStateBlockedReason(conflicted: conflicted, sequencer: sequencer) {
105	      return reason
106	    }
107	    if totalCount == 0 && vcs != "jj" {
108	      return "Nothing has changed in this workroom yet."
109	    }
110	    if vcs != "jj" && selectedCount == 0 {
111	      return "Select at least one file to commit."
112	    }
113	    return summaryBlockedReason(summary)
114	  }
115	
116	  /// Why the message-only verb — git's Amend, jj's Describe — is unavailable.
117	  ///
118	  /// The repo-state and summary rules, and deliberately NOT the file-count ones: both verbs rewrite a
119	  /// message and take no pathspec, so "select at least one file" is not a precondition for either.
120	  /// Sharing the rest is the point. The button used to enforce only its own summary check, which left
121	  /// it live over unresolved conflicts that the primary refused and the engine then rejected anyway —
122	  /// and it trimmed a different character set, so a summary of one newline blocked Commit while Amend
123	  /// would rewrite the last commit's message with it.
124	  static func messageOnlyBlockedReason(
125	    summary: String, conflicted: Bool, sequencer: String?
126	  ) -> String? {
127	    repoStateBlockedReason(conflicted: conflicted, sequencer: sequencer)
128	      ?? summaryBlockedReason(summary)
129	  }
130	
131	  /// The states of the repo itself that stop any commit verb, shared by both rules above.
132	  static func repoStateBlockedReason(conflicted: Bool, sequencer: String?) -> String? {
133	    if let sequencer {
134	      return "A \(sequencer) is in progress. Finish it in the terminal before committing."
135	    }
136	    // git refuses to commit unmerged paths outright. jj records conflicts inside commits and would
137	    // happily accept this, but "Commit" reading as "done" over unresolved conflicts is a UX decision,
138	    // not a capability one — so both backends say the same thing.
139	    if conflicted {
140	      return "Some files still have unresolved conflicts. Resolve them first."
141	    }
142	    return nil
143	  }
144	
145	  /// One trimming rule for every verb, so two buttons can never disagree about what "empty" means.
146	  static func summaryBlockedReason(_ summary: String) -> String? {
147	    summary.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).isEmpty
148	      ? "Write a summary to describe this change." : nil
149	  }
150	}

3	/// Record a commit: what will be included, the message, and the failure when there is one.
4	///
5	/// **Why a dialog rather than a box in the Changes pane.** Measured against the pane it would have
6	/// lived in: the composer is ~152pt and `InspectorPanePolicy.expandedMinHeight` leaves 86pt of body,
7	/// so at the pane's own drag floor the Commit button was below the fold. At a default third of a
8	/// 900pt window it left two file rows for git and one for jj — for a list whose entire job is letting
9	/// you decide whether committing is safe. Pinning it would also have meant switching Changes to fill
10	/// hosting, which disables the documented compress-and-scroll valve (`InspectorSplitView`), so a
11	/// short window would clip the button rather than scroll to it.
12	///
13	/// The dialog also deletes state rather than managing it: the draft and the selection live here for
14	/// the sheet's lifetime, so there is no per-workroom draft store to prune on delete, no recycled
15	/// workroom name inheriting last week's message, and no two windows racing one `Defaults` dictionary
16	/// (`AppStore` is per window).
17	///
18	/// The cost, accepted: this covers the diff you were reading.
19	struct CommitSheet: View {
20	  let pending: PendingCommit
21	  let onDismiss: () -> Void
22	
23	  @EnvironmentObject var store: AppStore
24	  private let theme = ThemeService.shared
25	
26	  @State private var summary = ""
27	  @State private var messageBody = ""
28	  /// EXCLUSIONS, not selections — see `CommitDraft.selected(from:excluding:)`. A file written while
29	  /// this sheet is open arrives checked; a file the user unticked stays unticked.
30	  @State private var excluded: Set<String> = []
31	  @State private var phase: Phase = .editing
32	  @State private var prefilled = false
33	  /// A parked merge/rebase/cherry-pick/revert/bisect in this worktree, resolved on appear.
34	  ///
35	  /// The engine refuses one of these outright, so leaving it out of `blockedReason` meant composing a
36	  /// whole message and pressing Commit to be told. Read once: finishing a merge is something the user
37	  /// does in the terminal, and re-polling for it would be a timer against the filesystem for a state
38	  /// that changes at human speed.
39	  @State private var sequencer: String?
40	  /// The commit `Amend last commit` would rewrite, so the message being replaced is visible BEFORE
41	  /// the click rather than recoverable only from the reflog afterwards.
42	  @State private var amendTarget: String?
43	  /// jj's stored description exactly as read, so an unedited Describe rewrites nothing.
44	  @State private var originalMessage: String?
45	  @FocusState private var summaryFocused: Bool
46	
47	  private enum Phase: Equatable {
48	    case editing
49	    /// Selected paths whose staged content this commit would discard, awaiting confirmation.
50	    case confirmingStagedLoss([String])
51	    case committing
52	    case failed(VCSFailureDialog)
53	    /// The commit LANDED but a later step failed. Terminal: the only honest action left is to close.
54	    /// Distinct from `.failed` because retrying here would record the work a second time, and the
55	    /// notice says so — so the buttons that would do it are disabled rather than merely discouraged.
56	    case landedThenFailed(VCSFailureDialog)
57	  }
58	
59	  /// The commit is on disk; nothing in this dialog can be pressed again without duplicating it.
60	  private var isSpent: Bool {
61	    if case .landedThenFailed = phase { return true }
62	    return false
63	  }
64	
65	  /// Hard cap on rendered rows, matching `ChangesPanel`'s. See `fileSection`.
66	  private static let renderCap = 200
67	
68	  private var isJJ: Bool { pending.vcs == "jj" }
69	  private var status: WorkroomStatus? { store.workroomStatuses[pending.sid] }
70	
71	  /// Every changed file, from whichever shape this backend reports.
72	  private var files: [ChangedFile] {
73	    guard let status else { return [] }
74	    if let workingCopy = status.jjWorkingCopy { return workingCopy.files }
75	    return status.changedFiles ?? []
76	  }
77	
78	  private var selectedFiles: [ChangedFile] {
79	    // jj commits the whole change, so the exclusion set is never applied to it.
80	    isJJ ? files : CommitDraft.selected(from: files, excluding: excluded)
81	  }
82	
83	  /// How many files the commit would record, WITHOUT building the filtered array.
84	  ///
85	  /// `body` asks this several times per evaluation — the caption, the button label, the blocked
86	  /// reason, the select-all glyph — and re-evaluates on every keystroke, so `selectedFiles.count`
87	  /// meant several full copies of the change set per typed character.
88	  private var selectedCount: Int {
89	    isJJ ? files.count : files.reduce(into: 0) { if !excluded.contains($1.path) { $0 += 1 } }
90	  }
91	
92	  private var blockedReason: String? {
93	    CommitDraft.blockedReason(
94	      vcs: pending.vcs, summary: summary, selectedCount: selectedCount,
95	      totalCount: files.count, conflicted: status?.conflicted ?? false, sequencer: sequencer)
96	  }
97	
98	  /// The secondary verb rewrites a message and takes no pathspec, so it answers to the repo-state and
99	  /// summary rules but not the file-count ones — see `CommitDraft.messageOnlyBlockedReason`.
100	  private var secondaryBlockedReason: String? {
101	    CommitDraft.messageOnlyBlockedReason(
102	      summary: summary, conflicted: status?.conflicted ?? false, sequencer: sequencer)
103	  }
104	
105	  var body: some View {
106	    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 14) {
107	      header
108	      fileSection
109	      messageSection
110	      amendTargetNotice
111	      if case .confirmingStagedLoss(let paths) = phase { stagedLossNotice(paths) }
112	      if case .failed(let dialog) = phase { CommitFailureNotice(dialog: dialog) }
113	      if case .landedThenFailed(let dialog) = phase { CommitFailureNotice(dialog: dialog) }
114	      Divider()
115	      buttons
116	    }
117	    .padding(20)
118	    .frame(width: 520)
119	    .onAppear(perform: prefill)
120	    // `children: .contain` is load-bearing: an identifier on a plain container makes SwiftUI treat it
121	    // as ONE element and swallow everything inside, which XCUITest then cannot reach. Same lesson
122	    // `VCSFailureSheet` records.
123	    .accessibilityElement(children: .contain)
124	    .accessibilityIdentifier("commit.sheet")
125	  }
126	
127	  private var header: some View {
128	    HStack(alignment: .firstTextBaseline, spacing: 8) {
129	      Text(isJJ ? "Describe this change" : "Commit changes")
130	        .font(.headline)
131	        .accessibilityIdentifier("commit.title")
132	      Spacer(minLength: 0)
133	      if !files.isEmpty {
134	        Text(countCaption)
135	          .font(.caption)
136	          .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
137	          .accessibilityIdentifier("commit.count")
138	      }
139	    }
140	  }
141	
142	  /// The primary button's label, which becomes an explicit confirmation while the staged-work
143	  /// warning is up so it can never read as an ordinary Commit.
144	  private var primaryLabel: String {
145	    if case .confirmingStagedLoss = phase { return "Commit anyway" }
146	    return CommitDraft.commitLabel(selectedCount: selectedCount, vcs: pending.vcs)
147	  }
148	
149	  private var countCaption: String {
150	    isJJ
151	      ? "\(files.count) file\(files.count == 1 ? "" : "s") in this change"
152	      : "\(selectedCount) of \(files.count) file\(files.count == 1 ? "" : "s")"
153	  }
154	
155	  // MARK: Files
156	
157	  @ViewBuilder private var fileSection: some View {
158	    if files.isEmpty {
159	      // jj can legitimately describe an empty change, so this is a note rather than a blocker there.
160	      Text(
161	        isJJ
162	          ? "This change has no file changes yet. You can still give it a message."
163	          : "Nothing has changed in this workroom yet."
164	      )
165	      .font(.callout).foregroundStyle(.secondary)
166	      .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
167	    } else {
168	      // Capped and lazy, for the reason `ChangesPanel.fileList` is: an accidental `node_modules` or
169	      // vendor drop is thousands of rows, and every one of `summary`, `messageBody` and `excluded` is
170	      // `@State` — so a non-lazy `ForEach` rebuilt the whole list on the main thread for each
171	      // keystroke. The count in the button label is the honest total either way: the cap limits what
172	      // is DRAWN, never what is committed.
173	      let shown = Array(files.prefix(Self.renderCap))
174	      VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 6) {
175	        if !isJJ { selectAllRow }
176	        ScrollView {
177	          LazyVStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 2) {
178	            ForEach(shown) { file in
179	              CommitFileRow(
180	                file: file, showsCheckbox: !isJJ,
181	                isIncluded: !excluded.contains(file.path),
182	                toggle: { toggle(file) },
183	                only: { excluded = Set(files.map(\.path)).subtracting([file.path]) })
184	            }
185	          }
186	          .padding(.vertical, 2)
187	        }
188	        .frame(maxHeight: 200)
189	        .background(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 6).fill(.quaternary.opacity(0.4)))
190	        if files.count > shown.count {
191	          // Never silent: the rows below the cap are still selected and still committed, and saying
192	          // so is the difference between a cap and a lie about what is about to be recorded.
193	          Text(
194	            "Showing the first \(shown.count) of \(files.count). All \(files.count) are included "
195	              + "unless you untick them."
196	          )
197	          .font(.caption).foregroundStyle(.tertiary)
198	          .fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)
199	          .accessibilityIdentifier("commit.renderCapNotice")
200	        }
201	        if isJJ {
202	          Text("jj commits the whole change. Splitting isn’t supported yet.")
203	            .font(.caption).foregroundStyle(.tertiary)
204	        }
205	      }
206	    }
207	  }
208	
209	  /// The staged-work warning: what committing is about to throw away, named, before it happens.
210	  ///
211	  /// `git commit --only` builds from the worktree, so for a file you staged with `git add -p` and
212	  /// then kept editing, the staged version is bypassed and gone — measured, with a clean
213	  /// `git status` afterwards and no other trace. This is not a refusal (committing from a partly
214	  /// staged file is legitimate), it is the difference between an informed choice and a silent loss.
215	  private func stagedLossNotice(_ paths: [String]) -> some View {
216	    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 6) {
217	      HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: 8) {
218	        Image(systemName: "exclamationmark.triangle.fill")
219	          .foregroundStyle(.orange).accessibilityHidden(true)
220	        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 4) {
221	          Text(
222	            paths.count == 1
223	              ? "1 file has staged changes that differ from the file on disk"
224	              : "\(paths.count) files have staged changes that differ from the files on disk"
225	          )
226	          .font(.subheadline.weight(.semibold))
227	          Text(
228	            "Committing records what is on disk, so the version you staged will be replaced. "
229	              + "Stage and commit it from the terminal instead if you meant to keep it."
230	          )
231	          .font(.caption).foregroundStyle(.secondary)
232	          .fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)
233	          Text(paths.prefix(5).joined(separator: ", ") + (paths.count > 5 ? ", …" : ""))
234	            .font(.system(.caption2, design: .monospaced))
235	            .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
236	            .textSelection(.enabled)
237	            .fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)
238	        }
239	      }
240	    }
241	    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
242	    .padding(10)
243	    .background(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 6).fill(Color.orange.opacity(0.08)))
244	    .accessibilityElement(children: .contain)
245	    .accessibilityIdentifier("commit.stagedLoss")
246	  }
247	
248	  /// The bulk affordance. Without it, "commit only this file" — an extremely common intent — costs
249	  /// one click per unwanted file.
250	  private var selectAllRow: some View {
251	    let allIncluded = excluded.isEmpty
252	    return Button {
253	      excluded = allIncluded ? Set(files.map(\.path)) : []
254	    } label: {
255	      HStack(spacing: 6) {
256	        Image(
257	          systemName: allIncluded
258	            ? "checkmark.square.fill" : (selectedCount == 0 ? "square" : "minus.square.fill")

Based on my review of the diff and the referenced call sites/functions:

**Analysis:**

1. **`gitHeadSubjectArgs()`** — hardcoded args (`git -c core.fsmonitor= log -1 --no-color --pretty=format:%h %s`); no user interpolation, no injection surface. Output (a commit subject, potentially attacker-influenced) flows only to SwiftUI `Text` and `.help(...)` — both inert sinks.

2. **`sequencerState()`** — returns one of six hardcoded labels ("merge", "cherry-pick", "rebase", "revert", "bisect") based on file-existence checks. The label is interpolated into the blocked-reason text; since it's a bounded enum from a hardcoded table, there's no injection.

3. **`worktreeGitDir(at:)`** — pre-existing, unchanged by this diff.

4. **`CommitDraft.message(preserving:)`** — pure string logic. No sinks. Correctness feature preserving byte-exact jj descriptions; no security impact.

5. **`UITestFixture.hugeChangeSet` / `amendTargetLabel`** — gated behind `#if DEBUG` + `UserDefaults` flag as documented in the `enabled` gate. Cannot activate in a release build.

6. **`renderCap` = 200** — the sibling-path gate concern here would be "cap on drawn rows lies about what is committed." The diff explicitly addresses this: `selectedCount` counts the full `files` array (not `shown`), the button label uses `selectedCount`, `selectedFiles` is not truncated, and a visible notice ("Showing the first 200 of N. All N are included…") is displayed. The commit request uses `selectedFiles`, which is unbounded. Verified: no divergence between what is drawn and what is committed.

7. **Prefill race** — `originalMessage` is only assigned when `summary.isEmpty && messageBody.isEmpty` at the check-time, preventing a stale stored value from causing a spurious no-op-describe early-return over user-typed content. The `commit(mode:)` no-op early-return only fires for `.describe` (jj), not `.amendMessage` (git), so amend can never be silently dropped.

8. **Amend target display** — a git commit subject is attacker-controllable, but it flows only into SwiftUI `Text`/`.help(...)`. `%h %s` (not `%B`) guarantees single-line, `--no-color` suppresses git-injected escapes. SwiftUI text views don't interpret ANSI/HTML. No sink.

9. **Sibling-path parity** — the parked-sequencer check is now added at the UI layer, matching the pre-existing engine-layer check in `VCSWriting.swift:1629`. Both `blockedReason` and `secondaryBlockedReason` receive the same `sequencer` value; parity holds.

No source→sink path with an effective bypass identified.
